official.deadline_central_display: Boren Fellowships: January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships: January 27, 2027 (both 5pm Eastern time)
official.deadline_note: Campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that applicants are asked to respect; selected applicants are notified in mid-to-late April.
official.status_note: The 2027-2028 Boren Scholarship and Boren Fellowship application cycles are open per the official Apply Now page.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: "Boren Scholarships and Fellowship funding is designed to cover the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses. The award is not all-inclusive." Approved program tuition and fees are eligible costs within the award.
official.funding_period: one-off award, tiered by programme duration
benefits: Fixed award tiers: $8,000 for 8-11 week summer programs (undergraduate STEM majors only), $12,500 for 12-24 weeks, $25,000 for 25-52 weeks

Covers the majority of overseas expenses: approved program tuition and fees, room and board, books and supplies, visa costs, Fly America Act compliant round-trip airfare, up to two checked bags, overseas health insurance and local transportation
Non-competitive eligibility for federal appointments until the service requirement is fulfilled, plus access to NSEPnet job listings
NSEP Service Team support, including resume reviews, career fairs, a mentorship program and advocacy with federal agency hiring officials
Annual Federal Employment Seminar in Washington, DC and access to the NSEP Alumni Association
eligibility: U.S. citizens at the time of the national application deadline
A high school graduate or GED holder, at least 18 years of age by the time the application is submitted

Matriculated for the duration of the funded program in an undergraduate or graduate degree program located within the United States and accredited by a body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education

Planning a continuous overseas program of at least 12 weeks (8 weeks for undergraduate STEM summer programs) outside Western Europe, Canada, Australia or New Zealand, in a destination of which the applicant is not a citizen
ROTC cadets, midshipmen and members of the Reserves or National Guard must be in inactive, non-drilling status for the duration of the funded program
requirements: Classroom language study must be a core element for the duration of the grant; overseas programs must contain at least 15-20 weekly language hours
Essay 1 on national security (max 800 words, single-spaced) and Essay 2 on motivation and public service careers (max 800 words for Scholarships, 1000 words for Fellowships)
Two letters of recommendation for Boren Scholarships (a third is optional); three for Boren Fellowships, with at least one from a research advisor if a research component is proposed
An alternate study abroad program is required for applicants choosing destinations marked with an asterisk or the languages Arabic, Mandarin or Russian
Unofficial transcript from the current U.S. institution is required in order to submit the application
documents: UNOFFICIAL transcript from the current U.S. institution showing name, institution, course titles and grades
UNOFFICIAL transcripts from up to two additional institutions where a previous degree was pursued or obtained
Description of the study abroad program: a screenshot or PDF from the program's website, or a scanned brochure, limited to no more than 5 pages
Letters of recommendation submitted by the recommenders through the online application system
Optional language proficiency evaluation by a language instructor, which does not count toward the letters requirement
selection_criteria: Preference is given by programme duration (25-52 weeks preferred), intensive study of a preferred language in a preferred overseas destination, the applicant's field of study, and longer-term interest in a federal career
Regional merit review panels of faculty and administrators from U.S. colleges and universities; final decision-making authority is held by DLNSEO
Selection preference is given to veterans when other factors are equivalent
coverage: Approved program tuition and fees, and home institution matriculation fees up to $2,500/semester ($5,000 overall cap)
Room and board (housing and food), books and supplies
Fly America Act compliant round-trip airfare at the lowest cost unrestricted class, and checked luggage (up to 2 bags)
Overseas health insurance, visa and overseas visa-related costs, local transportation
Select research-related expenses (Boren Fellows only) and cybersecurity costs including a burner laptop and/or phone or VPN (up to $500)
application_method: Visit the Apply Now page and start the application at apply.iie.org/borenscholarship or apply.iie.org/borenfellowship
Consult your Boren Awards campus representative at your institution for advice (you may still apply without one)
Watch the introductory webinar and review the official selection criteria
Complete the essays and study plan summary, and confirm recommenders
Submit the application through the online application system by the national deadline
official.application_route: Apply online through IIE's application system (apply.iie.org) by the national deadline for your track.
official.international_eligibility: No - applicants must be U.S. citizens at the time of the national application deadline
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Intensive classroom language study in a Boren-preferred language and preferred overseas destination; preferred fields of study are published on the eligibility page
official.research_requirement: Boren Fellows may pursue thesis or dissertation research abroad; letters of affiliation from overseas hosts are strongly advised when internships, coursework or research are proposed
official.duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study; 25-52 weeks preferred; minimum 12 weeks for most applicants (8 weeks minimum for undergraduate STEM summer programmes)
official.description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and graduate students (Boren Fellowships), paying a fixed grant designed to cover the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses in exchange for a commitment to at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security.

verification.notes: Award tiers ($8,000/$12,500/$25,000), the 2027-2028 open cycle and the January 20 / January 27, 2027 deadlines were read directly from borenawards.org Apply Now and Selecting an Eligible Study Program pages on 2026-10-10; the maximum published tier is recorded as the funding figure with the full tier structure preserved in benefits. No English-language requirement is published.

applicant_utility.summary: Boren pays a fixed tiered grant ($8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on programme length) that the programme itself says is not all-inclusive, so budget for the gap between the tier and your real costs. The two deadlines are separate and early: Fellowships January 20, Scholarships January 27, 2027, both 5pm Eastern. There is no interview stage - the essays are the entire audition - so tie your chosen language and country to a concrete U.S. national security and federal service story rather than generic study-abroad motivation.
applicant_utility.best_fit: U.S. citizen undergraduates and graduate students who can commit a full year to immersive language study in a preferred destination and genuinely intend a federal national-security career.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your proposed destination against the current preferred-destination list - Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand are always ineligible
For Arabic, Mandarin or Russian, or any asterisked destination, line up a viable alternate programme now
Confirm you can remain matriculated and delay graduation until the funded programme ends
Ask your campus representative about any earlier campus deadline
Model the shortfall between your award tier and your programme's actual cost before committing
common_rejection_risks: Programmes shorter than 12 weeks (8 weeks only for undergraduate STEM summer programmes) are ineligible
A language plan with fewer than 15-20 weekly classroom contact hours
Essays that never connect the language and region to U.S. national security and public service
Graduating before the funded period ends - Scholars and Fellows may not graduate until complete
Proposing study in a country of which you are a citizen
Study tours such as a semester at sea, which are not eligible
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award is explicitly not all-inclusive; you fund the difference between the tier and your actual programme cost, plus anything outside eligible costs such as non-approved travel.
document_audit: Unofficial transcripts must show your name, institution, course titles and grades - the unofficial transcript is required to submit
The study-programme description is capped at 5 pages
Recommenders submit their own letters through the system; even the optional third letter needs lead time
For asterisked destinations the alternate programme must be a real, viable plan, not a placeholder
alerts: Funding for programme expenses incurred after May 31, 2028 is contingent on availability and cannot be guaranteed at award
2027-cycle funding may be applied to programmes starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028
The one-year federal service obligation follows graduation - treat it as a career decision, not paperwork
Internships during the funded period may not be remunerated or conducted with any government; Fellows may not work as journalists abroad, even freelance or unpaid
Financial aid from other sources must be reported and may affect the grant (student loans do not)
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the online application at apply.iie.org with unofficial transcripts and letters by the national deadline, then await regional panel review with notifications in mid-to-late April.
